A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ContextLM and retain matching architecture and core experiments. All pages are readable, including v3's Appendix 7.1–7.7; v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2/Pythia training and downstream results, MT-Bench evaluations, architectural ablations, and attention analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds parameter-matched and MTP comparisons, AlpacaEval, LongBench, training curves, efficiency measurements, and pooling ablations.

M1.justification: The reported inference pseudocode changes: v1 invokes context prediction inside every token iteration, whereas v3 initializes it once and updates it at completed chunk boundaries, also revising boundary indexing. The encoder–predictor–decoder architecture, mean pooling, additive fusion, and cross-entropy objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds AlpacaEval 2.0 and LongBench's 0–4k subtasks, extending evaluation to longer-input single-document, multi-document, summarization, synthetic, and code/classification tasks. Existing training corpora and benchmarks remain. SciQ already appears in v1's result tables; correcting the prose's SIQA reference is not added coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds GPT2-PM baselines to perplexity and downstream comparisons across all four GPT-2 scales, plus a four-token MTP comparator at GPT2-XL scale (Table 6). v1 mentions parameter matching in its cost discussion but provides no corresponding performance rows; MTP is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 revises the chunk-size ablation from the default predictor depth to depth adjusted with chunk size to approximately match FLOPs and memory. New protocols include dynamic NTK-aware RoPE interpolation for LongBench, ordinary and length-controlled AlpacaEval win rates, and pooling comparisons at a 30k-step checkpoint. Existing main pretraining budgets and zero-/five-shot settings remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds an aggregation-strategy ablation (Table 13), matched-training Pythia convergence comparisons (Figure 6), and measured throughput/latency analysis (Table 10). It also materially revises the chunk-size study. Earlier predictor-depth, encoder/decoder-split, block-size, and attention analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 1 changes the reported parameter-scaling fit from zero-offset power laws to power laws with additive floors of 13.1 and 13.0, revising the statistical model used to summarize scaling. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original perplexity/downstream rows and MT-Bench averages remain unchanged. v3 adds PM/MTP results, AlpacaEval win rates of 54.48% and 54.01% length-controlled, LongBench scores of 23.32 versus 20.21, and appendix analysis results. Parameter savings change from 38% to 39%; the revised chunk experiment favors w=4 rather than w=2 under different controls. The earlier below-5% GPU-memory-overhead observation disappears. Table 6's ARC-Challenge value of 21.6 conflicts with 21.4 retained in Table 12.

T1.justification: v3 Table 10 extends the existing complexity analysis with separate inference orders, O(Td) for the token decoder and O((T/w)d) for the context predictor, and combined overhead expressions. The principal gradient derivations and training/memory orders are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains predictive context embeddings that improve autoregressive language modeling. v3 explicitly claims downstream advantages under equivalent parameter counts and foregrounds quantified parameter efficiency. Its conclusion drops v1's stronger assertion that no backbone architecture changes are required, retaining compatibility with token-level evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 explains the preferred 0/12 split through deeper decoder integration of context, adds interpretations distinguishing context modeling from extra parameters and MTP, and motivates mean pooling through comparable ablation performance. It also replaces v1's blanket numerical descriptions of downstream gains with more qualified scale-dependent discussion. These refine the existing interpretation without introducing substantial failure or limitation analysis.

D1.justification: Appendices 7.1–7.3 newly disclose GPT-2 AdamW betas, clipping and warmup, explicit Pythia hyperparameters, A100 80GB hardware, and approximately 3,594/5,375 GPU-hours for the 1B/1.4B models. Efficiency hardware and the pooling checkpoint are also specified. These substantially expand documentation without establishing changed main training settings. Existing access links remain; the relocated GPT-2 table drops its layer-count column.

R1.justification: v3 substantially reframes related work around modeling above versus below tokens. It adds discussions of DLCM, CALM, MegaByte, and JEPA applications while removing discussions including BlockFormer, SegFormer, and LongNet. The distinctions drawn against latent and hierarchical predecessors change substantively; bibliographic updates to retained works are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, experimental discussion, and related work are extensively rewritten. Architecture components receive separate subsections, analysis becomes a standalone section, and complexity, training details, and full GPT-2 results move into an organized appendix. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v3 introduces a main summary table, expands comparisons with PM rows, and adds benchmark, efficiency, hyperparameter, and pooling tables plus training curves. Figure 4 merges the earlier ablation and length plots and revises the chunk-size panel; Figure 1 is redrawn and repositioned. Full GPT-2 tables move to the appendix, where Tables 9 and 11 duplicate the same perplexity comparison.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens experimental credibility by adding explicit parameter-matched performance controls and an MTP comparison, addressing important alternative explanations for v1's gains. LongBench, convergence and efficiency analyses broaden validation, while the appendix materially improves reproducibility. Missing run uncertainty, duplicated tables, and the inconsistent ARC-Challenge entry remain weaknesses, but they do not outweigh the stronger evidence supporting the central contribution.
